small_guidance:
- The inner loop iterates `oh` sequentially with a `tl.dot(BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC) x (BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_W)` per (kh,kw); BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_IC=64, BLOCK_W up to 256 — try adding configs that split BLOCK_OC (64) and use BLOCK_W=32/64 with num_warps=4 to reduce register pressure, and add num_stages=4 variants for the OH loop.
- Parallelize across `oh` as a third grid axis (one program per (n, oh-tile, ow-tile)) and do a final reduction/sum across oh via atomic_add or a second small kernel — currently each program serializes OH=256 iterations, which is the dominant latency source.
- Hoist the `w_tile` load out of the OH loop (weights are reused for every oh); precompute and cache the 9 (kh,kw) weight tiles in registers/SRAM before entering the OH loop.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a scatter-add formulation for ConvTranspose2d: one program per (N, IC-tile, IH, IW-tile) computes `input × weight` outer products and scatters into a per-program partial output that is min-reduced across OC and sum-reduced across OH on the fly. Since the output is only (N,1,1,OW), keep an OW-sized accumulator per program and use atomics for cross-program OH/IC contributions — or better, fuse so each program owns a full (n, ow-tile) column and loops over (ic, ih, iw) gathering, which exactly inverts the current gather and exposes more parallelism.
- Make OH a parallel grid axis: launch (N, OH, ow-tiles), have each program compute the min-over-OC at that (n,oh,ow), then do a tree/atomic sum-reduce over OH into a (N,1,1,OW) buffer, then a tiny epilogue kernel applies GELU+bias. This eliminates the serial OH=256 loop that's currently bottlenecking the kernel.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) layout for the input and a (KH,KW,IC,OC) weight layout so the GEMM-K axis (IC) is contiguous; with IC=64 and OC=128 the per-(kh,kw) GEMM is tiny — batch all 9 (kh,kw) into the K dimension of one larger `tl.dot` to amortize.
